mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring threshold activation.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 4.5%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 2000 thousand units signals robust consumer demand for durable goods, increasing corporate revenue expectations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when HOUST > 2000, or the correlation between HOUST > 2000 and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 4.5%) and low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 200) indicates stable monetary conditions that support equity valuation expansion, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (FEDFUNDS < 4.5 and CPIAUCSL < 200) fails to produce positive returns in more than 40% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression of 20-day returns on both proxies is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE increase > 0.2% over 3 months) signals labor market deterioration that triggers equity sell-offs, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances during late-cycle expansions with UNRATE increase > 0.2% in 3 months, or the return distribution under this condition is not significantly different from baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: GDP level exceeding 16000 billion dollars indicates robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 > 16000, or the correlation between GDPC1 > 16000 and positive returns is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4.5% consistently reduces short-term financing costs, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days without threshold activation.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 4.5%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production falling below 100 (index 2017=100) signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or the correlation between INDPRO < 100 and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% over 1 month) combined with low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.5%) indicates a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE < 4.5%) fails to produce positive returns in more than 40% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression of 20-day returns on both proxies is not significant (p > 0.05).
